rationale: PY-D13: BOTH halves now. Round 7 (lane-side): the resolution verdict's `references` (1,332) and `extends` (105) UNEXPLAINED targets are dominated by alias-bound routes — `t.Callable`, `t.Self`, `t.Protocol`, `nn.Module` — where `t`/`nn` is a name the file bound with `as` and the module's real name is nowhere on the edge; the analyzer parsed the alias all along and published it on no relation, and for `from X import Z as W` it lost the binding one layer deeper, recording only the imported `Z`. It rode the edge as `metadata.importedAs`. Round 17 (store half): the ROW the worker projects now carries the binding too — the from-import publishes `itemBindings` per item and the projection emits `alias`, so `brain_import.imported_as` receives `OD` for `from collections import OrderedDict as OD` instead of staying NULL for every language (the projection dropped `alias` while the indexer read `imp.alias ?? imp.localName`, so neither key ever existed on the AST path). The `expectImports` rows below are the FALSIFIER for the round-17 publication — they are what catches the mutant that removes it, since the standalone seam pin is not part of this battery. The plain imports are the control in both channels: `importedAs` must not be invented on the edge where the bound name is already the imported name, and `itemBindings` must stay EMPTY on such a row.

expectRelationships.note: `import typing as t` — the namespace binding `t` is what the file's `t.Callable` routes name
the same shape, different spelling, so the rule is not keyed on one alias
THE FROM-IMPORT CASE: `from collections import OrderedDict as OD` binds `OD`, and before round 7 the item list carried only the IMPORTED name — the bound name appeared on no edge at all
the un-aliased item is still published as an edge (the control's positive row)
the un-aliased namespace import still emits its edge

expectImports.note: ROUND 17's falsifier: the from-import ROW carries the bound name per item, which is what `src/ast/pool-worker.ts` now projects into `alias` and `src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts` writes into `brain_import.imported_as`. Whole-array equality on `itemBindings` (the matcher compares arrays by sorted JSON) means this row also fails if a SECOND, invented binding appears here.

WHY THE BINDING RIDES THE ITEM AND NOT THE ROW: one statement binds two names and only the SECOND is aliased, so a single row-level `alias` cannot express it (and `alias` on the row is exactly what the pre-round-17 design would have had to invent). `items` keeps the IMPORTED names — `field`, never `dataclass_field` — because those are what the `module:item` edge target spells and what the resolution verdict counts.

THE CONTROL, over-claim direction: an un-aliased item must leave `itemBindings` EMPTY — a binding that merely repeats the imported name is noise a store consumer has to filter, and `null`/absent and `[]` are the same statement here.

forbidRelationships.note: OVER-CLAIM DIRECTION: `import os` binds `os`, which is already the imported name the target spells — publishing it would be noise, not a fact
the same for an un-aliased from-import item
the LOSS DIRECTION, pinned as a forbid: the edge must name the IMPORTED name (`collections:OrderedDict`), never the bound alias, because `OD` is not a module attribute any file declares
